findings: Each document is assigned a fixed home jurisdiction at creation time (EU or US) based on the owning customer's contract; all content — snapshots, CRDT op log, and audit log — is stored and durably replicated only within that jurisdiction's infrastructure, never cross-region.
Concurrent editing uses a CRDT (Yjs/Automerge-style) rather than server-mediated OT/locking, so concurrent ops commute and merge deterministically with no central lock and no data loss.

Clients apply their own edits locally and optimistically before any network round trip, then broadcast ops asynchronously — this is what delivers sub-200ms perceived latency, independent of server or cross-region RTT.

A collaborator physically outside the document's home region (e.g., a US user on an EU-owned doc) still has their live-editing WebSocket session routed to the EU regional cluster — compute follows data, not the user — so EU content is never copied into US infrastructure; that user simply accepts extra network latency as an explicit tradeoff.

The audit log is not a separate write path: it is the same durable, append-only, hash-chained op log that drives CRDT sync, so there is a single source of truth and no dual-write divergence between 'what synced' and 'what got audited'.

Durability is achieved via synchronous multi-AZ (or multi-region-within-jurisdiction, e.g. eu-west-1 + eu-central-1) replication of the op log before an edit is acknowledged, bounding loss to a same-jurisdiction AZ failure, not a full regional outage.

On a full regional outage, the system does not fail over the write path to another jurisdiction (that would violate residency); instead clients queue ops in a durable local outbox (e.g. IndexedDB) and keep editing offline, replaying and CRDT-merging once the home region recovers — live cross-user sync is explicitly unavailable during the outage rather than faked.

A global, jurisdiction-agnostic control plane (org-to-region routing table, user directory) is the only component replicated worldwide, since it carries no regulated document content, and it is what lets one global entry point route every session to the correct regional cluster.

Fan-out of live ops to connected collaborators runs on a pub/sub broadcast tier decoupled from the durable log write, so viewer/collaborator count on a hot document doesn't bottleneck durable-write throughput.
CRDT tombstones/causal metadata are garbage-collected periodically once all replicas acknowledge causal stability, bounding long-term storage growth from concurrent-edit storms.

The design explicitly accepts and documents that true zero-RPO cross-region failover for EU data is impossible under the residency constraint — elevated unavailability during a full EU regional outage is a deliberate, disclosed tradeoff rather than a hidden gap.
